# RapidCAM

> RapidCAM (https://rapidcam.app) is a free, browser-based parametric 2D CAD +
> CAM application for CNC mills, rotary (4th-axis) machines, and lasers. Its
> project format, `.rcam`, is plain JSON with a published JSON Schema, and is
> explicitly designed so that automated tools — including LLMs — can author
> valid design files.

**Can you only fetch a single URL?** Some AI tools cannot follow links found
in a fetched page. Fetch [the single-file bundle](https://rapidcam.app/llms-full.txt)
instead — this index plus the full format guide, the JSON Schema, and the AI
integration guide, inlined as one plain-text document.

## File format (.rcam)

- [Format guide](https://rapidcam.app/docs/rcam-format-v3.md): the human- and
  AI-readable authoring guide — point-key vocabulary, constraint semantics,
  CAM operations, and gotchas the schema can't express
- [JSON Schema, draft 2020-12](https://rapidcam.app/schema/rcam-v3.schema.json):
  the machine-readable contract (this URL is also the schema's `$id`)
- [Examples index](https://rapidcam.app/examples/index.json): bundled golden
  example projects, each validated against the schema on every commit; fetch
  any listed file at `https://rapidcam.app/examples/<name>`
- [AI integration guide](https://rapidcam.app/docs/ai-integration.md): every
  way an AI can work with RapidCAM — the in-app assistant loop, this index,
  the headless CLI, and the MCP server — plus authoring tips

## Parametric features (generators)

- `features[]` in `.rcam`: geometry produced by a built-in generator (box,
  box-joint, spur gear, ...) that stays re-editable — `{id, generatorId,
  params, paramExprs?, groupId, offset}`.
- `paramExprs` (optional) holds an expression per param, evaluated against
  document `variables` and `stock` (the stock thickness); `params` holds the
  last resolved values as cache/fallback for params with no expression, or
  whose expression fails to evaluate.
- Features regenerate automatically when a variable they reference changes
  (and are self-healed on file open if `params` doesn't match what the
  expressions currently resolve to).
- Entity ids stay stable across a regeneration, so CAM operations,
  constraints, and dimensions that reference generated geometry survive a
  parameter edit.
- `keyIds` (optional) maps generator-assigned stable keys (e.g. "front-wall")
  to entity ids; keyed entities keep their ids by key rather than by emit
  position, so references survive output reordering and partial deletes.

## Parametric CAM operations

- `operations[]` may carry `paramExprs` too — an expression per **numeric op
  field**, keyed by field name: `{"depth": "-stock", "feedrate": "baseFeed*1.2"}`.
  Evaluated against `variables` and `stock` before every solve, then clamped to
  the field's valid range.
- Always also emit the plain numeric field (`depth`, `feedrate`, ...): it is the
  last resolved value and the fallback when a field has no expression or its
  expression fails. A file never needs an expression evaluated to load.
- Bare numbers in an expression are **millimetres** (as in variable, dimension,
  and feature formulas) regardless of `displayUnit`.
- Nested fields take either key spelling: `"tabCount"`/`"tabs.count"`,
  `"leadInLen"`/`"leadIn.length"`. Ignored while `tabs`/`leadIn`/`leadOut` is absent.
- `"depth": "-stock"` is the common case — a profile that always cuts through
  whatever the stock currently is.

## Laser jobs from layers

- A **layer** may carry a `laser` recipe — `{kind?, feedrate, laserPower,
  laserPasses, kerfWidth?, side?, airAssist?}` — so a design describes how each
  colour is cut: cut on black, score on red, engrave on blue.
- `feedrate`/`laserPower`/`laserPasses` are **live**: any operation whose
  `entityIds` all sit on that layer takes them at toolpath time, so re-tuning a
  layer re-tunes everything on it. An operation spanning several layers keeps
  its own settings, and `"laserOverride": true` opts one out entirely.
- `kind` (`"cut"|"score"|"engrave"|"fill"`) is read when operations are BUILT,
  not applied live — a cut, an engrave and a fill emit different geometry, so
  retyping an existing operation at export would not match its preview. A layer
  with a recipe but no `kind` tunes the operations that cut it without being a
  job of its own.
- Emitting layers with kinds and NO `operations` is a valid, compact way to
  describe a laser job: the user presses **Toolpaths from Layers** and gets one
  operation per layer, in layer order, named after the layer.
- Hidden layers (`"visible": false`) and workholding layers (`"fixture": true`)
  are never cut when a job is built FROM LAYERS. An operation that names
  workholding geometry explicitly still cuts it — pre-flight warns
  (`machined-fixture`) rather than dropping the cut silently.
- A clamp's height above the stock top comes from the layer's `fixtureHeight`,
  or from the shape's own `fixtureHeight` when clamps of different heights share
  a layer. Unset at both levels means full-height: it blocks every pass.
- Kerf direction is automatic unless you set `side`: a contour enclosed by
  another on the same layer is treated as a hole and compensated inward while
  the outline goes outward, so both finish at the drawn size.
## Authoring tips for LLMs

- All lengths are millimetres and all angles are radians (CCW), regardless of
  the file's `displayUnit`. The world frame is Y-up.
- You do not need exact coordinates: emit rough positions plus constraints and
  dimensions, and RapidCAM's parametric solver snaps the geometry exact.
- Declare `"version": 3` and validate your output against the schema before
  presenting it to a user.
- Opening a file in RapidCAM reports schema, solver, and CAM lint problems;
  iterate on that feedback rather than aiming for a perfect first attempt.
- Agents on the user's machine with a RapidCAM checkout can run those same
  checks headlessly (CLI: `npm run cli -- validate|post|render|open|decode`)
  or as MCP tools (`npm run mcp`), including `open` — which delivers a
  validated design straight into the user's browser via a share-link URL —
  and `decode`, which turns a copied share link back into .rcam JSON. See
  the AI integration guide above.
